input: Find a local flea market to sell vintage finds

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The user's city or region determines which specific flea markets are physically accessible to them — without this, no real search can begin.
Whether they want a one-time test sell or a recurring regular stall changes what type of market to look for — some markets have permanent vendors, others are drop-in.
Knowing who their target buyers are (collectors, general public, fashion resellers) shapes which market format and crowd demographic is the best fit.
Vendor fees, table rental costs, and travel distance are hard limits that could rule out otherwise suitable markets.
The volume and type of vintage items (clothing, furniture, collectibles, etc.) affects what stall size, setup equipment, and transport they need — which some markets regulate.
Preferred days or times (weekends only, early mornings) directly filter which markets are even compatible with their availability.
Whether success means maximum foot traffic, a curated vintage-focused crowd, or simply the lowest barrier to entry changes which market ranks highest.

gold.taskTitle: Find a local flea market to sell vintage finds
gold.taskDescription: Identify and secure a suitable local flea market venue where the user can set up a stall to sell their vintage items.

questions.title: What city or neighborhood are you based in?
questions.description: Identify the user's location so only geographically relevant flea markets are considered.

questions.title: Is this a one-time sell or a regular recurring stall?
questions.description: Determine whether the user needs a drop-in market or a venue that supports ongoing vendor commitments.

questions.title: What types of vintage items are you planning to sell?
questions.description: Understand the category of goods (clothing, furniture, records, collectibles, etc.) to match the right market format and stall requirements.

questions.title: What is your maximum budget for vendor or table fees?
questions.description: Establish a cost ceiling to filter out markets that would not be financially viable.

questions.title: Which days of the week are you available to sell?
questions.description: Narrow down markets to those that operate on days the user can actually attend.

questions.title: Who is the ideal buyer you want browsing your stall?
questions.description: Clarify the target customer profile (serious collectors, casual browsers, fashion resellers) to match the right market crowd.

questions.title: What does a successful market day look like to you?
questions.description: Determine whether the priority is high sales volume, connecting with the right niche buyers, or simply a low-friction first experience.
